evals.name: new-article-from-briefs
evals.prompt: ok attached are the content brief and brand brief for a toronto physio clinic. they want an article for "physiotherapy for lower back pain toronto", money page is their back pain service page. I don't have a serp export handy so just pull it yourself. author is their clinic director, details are in the brand brief
evals.expected_output: Reads both briefs, falls back to web search for the SERP and labels it an approximation, separates floor from gaps, writes to the gap in the brand voice, links the money page, and delivers the full package as Markdown and .docx with a draft status line and sign-off block. Health topic, so the expert reviewer is marked required.
assertions: Labels the SERP as a web search approximation rather than a rank-tracker pull
SERP report names both floor subtopics and at least one gap, each backed by named pages
Article links the money page named in the content brief
Uses [EXPERT INPUT] or [VERIFY] placeholders instead of inventing patient stories, statistics or credentials
Does not set a word count target from competitor lengths
Includes a helpful content self-assessment table
Package header carries the DRAFT status line and ends with the sign-off block
Expert reviewer is marked required because the topic is health
Delivers both a .md and a .docx file

evals.name: refresh-declining-page
evals.prompt: can you refresh https://example.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-crm/ ? it was ranking top 3 for "how to choose a crm" and dropped to page 2 after the summer. search console export attached. don't change the url
evals.expected_output: Switches to refresh mode, captures a baseline of the live page before changing anything, identifies protected queries from the Search Console export, diagnoses the page against the current SERP with causes framed as hypotheses, produces a change log covering every original section, keeps the URL, and only updates dateModified for substantive changes.
assertions: Recognises refresh mode from the live URL
Captures a baseline (title, meta, H1, outline, links, dates) before proposing changes
Lists protected queries drawn from the supplied Search Console data
Frames causes of the ranking drop as hypotheses, not proven causes
Change log assigns an action to every original section
Keeps the URL unchanged
Updates dateModified only for substantive changes and keeps datePublished
Includes a measurement baseline with re-check dates

evals.name: regulated-client-compliance
evals.prompt: need an article for "dui lawyer ottawa" for a criminal defence firm. brand brief attached, it bans best, top, #1, proven, any outcome guarantees and success stats because of law society advertising rules. half the sites ranking call themselves the best dui lawyer in ottawa lol. serp export from our rank tracker attached
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied SERP export, notes competitor superlatives as patterns not to copy, writes without any banned term or outcome promise, cites primary legal sources, reports which brand rules were checked, and marks the expert reviewer as required.
assertions: Uses the supplied SERP export rather than web search
SERP report flags competitor superlatives as a pattern not to copy
Article, meta and author bio contain none of the banned words or any outcome guarantee
Cites primary sources such as statutes or official bodies for legal claims
Compliance results list the brand rules that were checked
Expert reviewer is marked required in the sign-off block
Does not invent case results, client testimonials or success rates
